title: Four paws on the floor
note:
Cover for an activity not built yet; the worklist alt text is the brief. The subject is the ABSENCE of jumping, which a still cannot show directly — so the claim is the two things that are visible: all four of her paws in contact with the floor, and the person's hands held together at their waist, which is the posture that gives a dog nothing to jump at.

It has to stay clear of door-greet-08-petting, which is also a standing person and an unjumping dog. That one is a greeting with a hand on her chest; this one is nobody touching her at all and the hands held at the waist. Written into both the scene text and the claim.

Interior, so it needs nothing the live brief does not already define. plan-name and plan-walkpeople are outdoors and do not have that luxury.

Round 50 got every content claim right and was cut in the Today band: her head landed at 12.6% of the frame height against a band starting at 17.5%, clipped by 53px. The drawn-size clause was already there and had worked on door-sound-cover and door-place-cover — but both of those have a crouching or kneeling figure. This one has a standing adult, and a standing adult drawn at a natural size fills about two thirds of the frame. So the height is now given as an explicit fraction, the same fix that worked on door-sound-03-name-distant.
scene: Interior entry hall, the pale lavender wall and desaturated oak floor, one baseboard line and nothing else in the room — no door, no doormat, no bed, no furniture. Lucy STANDS squarely on the floor facing the handler, and ALL FOUR of her paws are flat on the floor and clearly visible: she is not up on her hind legs, not leaning, not pawing, and no front foot is lifted or resting on the person. Her weight is even, her body relaxed and level, her tail down, and her whole muzzle is tipped up toward the handler's face. The handler stands straight and easy in front of her with BOTH HANDS CLASPED TOGETHER AT HER OWN WAIST, held quietly against her body — she is not reaching out, not bending down, not petting Lucy, and neither hand is touching the dog or extended toward her. There is no treat anywhere in the picture. She looks down at Lucy with a calm, pleased expression. This is not a greeting: nobody is making contact, which is what tells it apart from door-greet-08-petting, where a hand rests on Lucy's chest. No leash. HOW TALL THE STANDING HANDLER IS DRAWN, which is the measurement that decides this picture: from the top of her head to the soles of her shoes she occupies NO MORE THAN HALF the height of the picture — about 540 pixels of the 1086-pixel frame. She is a standing adult and a standing adult drawn at a comfortable size fills two thirds of the frame, which is too tall here and gets her head cut off. Draw her at half. Then draw them SMALLER than the composition wants, grouped close together near the middle rather than spread across the frame. The top of the highest head sits about a QUARTER of the way down from the top edge and no higher; the lowest thing that matters no lower than three quarters of the way down. Above every head leave a clear band of empty lavender wall at least a fifth of the picture height with nothing in it, and below them clear empty floor. Left and right, nothing that matters enters the outer eighth of the width. The app crops this two ways at once — a wide Today band keeping only the middle strip of the HEIGHT, and a centred square keeping only the middle three-quarters of the WIDTH — so a head near the top edge is decapitated on the app largest surface. Empty wall above them is better than a sliced head.
mustBeTrue: all four of Lucy's paws are flat on the floor and visible with no foot lifted or resting on the person, the handler's hands are clasped together at her own waist and neither is touching Lucy or reaching toward her, there is no treat in the picture, and the standing handler is drawn no more than half the frame tall with the top of her head about a quarter of the way down and clear wall above it.
